newsitem.title: USA: AIG Q4 general insurance net premiums up.
newsitem.headline: AIG Q4 general insurance net premiums up.

text.p: American International Group Inc said general insurance worldwide net premiums written rose 7.1 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 before the impact of foreign exchange and rose 9.6 percent for the full year.
Including the effect of foreign exchange, general insurance worldwide net premiums written rose 5.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 and 6.7 percent for the year.
American International said the company achieved an underwriting profit of $399 million in 1996 and a combined ratio of 96.87 percent compared to 97.04 percent in 1995.
For the fourth quarter, the combined ratio was 97.54, compared to 97.45 in 1995's fourth quarter.
Net catastrophe losses totalled $79 million in 1996, compared to $100 million the prior year.
Domestic net premiums written rose 7.7 percent for the quarter and 8.8 percent for the full year 1996.

"In a highly competitive domestic market, AIG's focus on specialty products, new product development, efficient distribution and tight expense management enabled us to perform well," AIG chairman M.R. Greenberg said.
"Our domestic personal lines business made excellent progress in the year, and our new joint venture in Arizona with 20th Century Industries is also proceeding very well."
AIG said its United Guaranty Corp mortgage guaranty insurance subsidiary reported an increase in operating income of 10.3 percent for the year to $147.2 million.
The foreign property-casualty business reported an increase in net premiums written of 5.9 percent before the impact of foreign exchange and up 11 percent for the year.
After the impact of foreign exchange, however, foreign net premiums written rose only 0.5 percent in the fourth quarter, AIG said.
"Many new overseas initiatives were inaugurated in 1996, and these should benefit future earnings, as will the insurance trade agreement recently concluded with Japan," Greenberg said.

AIG said it added $160 million and $714 million to its general insurance net loss and loss adjustment reserves for the quarter and full year, respectively, bringing the total of those reserves to $20.4 billion at year-end.
The loss reserve increase for the year was consistent with the increase in net premiums earned, AIG said.
